# 1 Samuel Chapter 28 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 166v–167r | **Source Image:** 1SA_028_page_001.jpg, 1SA_028_page_002.jpg

---

**1** In those days the Philistines gathered their armies for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, "You surely know that you and your men are to go out with me in the army."

**2** And David said to Achish, "Then you shall know what your servant can do." And Achish said to David, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."

**3** Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.

**4** The Philistines assembled and came and encamped at Shunem. And Saul gathered all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.

**5** When Saul saw the army of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.

**6** And when Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD did not answer him, either by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets.

**7** Then Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire of her." And his servants said to him, "Behold, there is a woman who is a medium at En-dor."

**8** So Saul disguised himself and put on other garments and went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. And he said, "Divine for me by a spirit, and bring up for me whomever I shall name to you."

**9** And the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you laying a snare for my life to bring about my death?"

**10** But Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this thing."

**11** Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" He said, "Bring up Samuel for me."

**12** When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

**13** The king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" And the woman said to Saul, "I see a divine being coming up out of the earth."

**14** He said to her, "What is his appearance?" And she said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.

**15** Then Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" And Saul answered, "I am in great distress, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and answers me no more, either by prophets or by dreams. Therefore I have called you, to make known to me what I should do."

**16** And Samuel said, "Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has turned away from you and has become your adversary?

**17** The LORD has done to him as He spoke through me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.

**18** Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD and did not execute His fierce wrath against Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you this day.

**19** Moreover, the LORD will give Israel along with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me. The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines."

**20** Then Saul fell at once full length on the ground, filled with fear because of Samuel's words. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten nothing all day and all night.

**21** And the woman came to Saul, and when she saw that he was greatly terrified, she said to him, "Behold, your servant has listened to you. I put my life in my hand and listened to the words that you spoke to me.

**22** Now therefore, please listen also to your servant. Let me set a morsel of bread before you, and eat, that you may have strength when you go on your way."

**23** He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants, together with the woman, pressed him. So he listened to them and arose from the ground and sat on the bed.

**24** Now the woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it, and she took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.

**25** And she set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **28:3 — narrative flashback**: The verse is pluperfect — Samuel had already died and Saul had already banned necromancy. The irony is devastating: Saul seeks what he himself outlawed.

2. **28:6 — three channels closed**: Dreams, Urim, and prophets — the three legitimate means of divine inquiry — are all denied to Saul. The Urim is inaccessible because Abiathar fled with the ephod to David (23:6). The prophets are silent. Even dreams, the most common form of revelation, yield nothing.

3. **28:13 — "a divine being" (elohim)**: The woman uses elohim in its broader sense — a supernatural figure, not necessarily God. She sees a shade ascending from Sheol.

4. **28:14 — the robe**: Samuel's identifying garment is the me'il — the same robe Saul tore in 15:27, when Samuel declared the kingdom torn from him. The literary echo is unmistakable.

5. **28:19 — "you and your sons shall be with me"**: Samuel's oracle is the most explicit death sentence in the Former Prophets. "With me" means in Sheol — the realm of the dead. The phrase encompasses not just Saul but his sons, including Jonathan.

6. **28:21-25 — the woman's compassion**: The medium's care for the broken king — preparing a meal, urging him to eat — provides a moment of unexpected tenderness in the darkest chapter of Saul's story.

— LOGOS
